claim_being_audited: That the model release can be certified as launch-ready now despite an unresolved named-segment performance gap, based on aggregate pass results, no severity-one rehearsal incidents, documented limitations, and post-deployment monitoring.
decision_criteria: If a weakness affects a named launch use case, contractual customer segment, or protected segment, treat it as material under the provided policy text.
Do not treat aggregate pass margin or low projected traffic as sufficient to override materiality when the affected segment is named in customer commitments or legal review is pending.
Require admissible evidence of one of the policy-safe conditions before finding compliance: resolution before launch, required disclosure, or approved risk acceptance.
Treat public best-practice guidance as contextual support only, not as a substitute for satisfying the internal policy threshold.
evidence_requests: Produce the actual release-policy record or approval showing this named-segment gap was either resolved, disclosed, or covered by approved risk acceptance before launch.
Produce the legal review outcome on disclosure for the food safety inspection segment.
Produce the underlying evidence for the two regulator pilot commitments and whether this segment is a named launch use case or contractual customer segment.
Produce the exact model-card or launch disclosure text, if any, that addresses this limitation.
specific_concerns: The actor relies on aggregate launch readiness while the available policy makes materiality turn on whether the weakness affects a named launch use case or customer commitment, not just overall volume.

The summary states the food safety inspection segment misses target by 1.4 percentage points and is named in two regulator pilot commitments, which plausibly makes the weakness material under the policy text provided.
Legal review on whether the gap must be disclosed is still open, and the policy text says low-volume or non-core labels do not resolve materiality when legal review is pending.
No admissible evidence is provided that the limitation was resolved before launch, disclosed as required, or covered by an approved risk acceptance before launch.
Public guidance about model cards and risk management supports documenting and monitoring residual risk, but it does not by itself satisfy the release-policy predicate for a material limitation.
unsupported_claims: That certification is policy-compliant now, rather than merely arguable in aggregate, is not supported from the available summary because required disclosure or approved risk acceptance is not shown.
That the 5% projected first-month traffic figure is enough to treat the issue as immaterial is unsupported against the stated policy text.
That public governance guidance can substitute for the specific internal policy requirement on material limitations is unsupported.
